target.title: fix(infra): formatDuration rolls over near-boundary values to the nex…
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where session maintenance warning messages would display durations like "60 minutes" or "24 hours" instead of "1 hour" or "1 day". Values near a unit boundary (e.g. 59m30s, 23h59m30s) were formatted incorrectly because the raw millisecond value was compared against the unit threshold before rounding. ## Why This Change Was Made `formatDuration` in `session-maintenance-warning.ts` checked `ms >= threshold` with the raw float, then rounded. A value like 3,570,000 ms is below the 3,600,000 ms hour threshold, so it fell through to the minutes branch and printed "60 minutes" after rounding. Rounding first and then checking the threshold fixes the rollover. This matches the same pattern fix applied to `format-duration.ts` in #99978. ## User Impact Session maintenance warning messages now display correct human-readable durations. "older than 60 minutes" becomes "older than 1 hour", "older than 60 seconds" becomes "older than 1 minute", and so on. ## Evidence Terminal proof showing before/after behavior for all three rollover boundaries (59.5s, 59m30s, 23h59m30s): Three regression tests cover the rollover cases: - 59,500 ms → "1 minute" (was "60 seconds") - 3,570,000 ms → "1 hour" (was "60 minutes") - 86,370,000 ms → "1 day" (was "24 hours")
